title: The Dream That Dreams Itself Awake

features.name: the waking animal
features.desc-on-touch: a creature—kangaroo, perhaps, or something that only exists in the overlap between sleep and day—that has noticed itself is being dreamed; it is watching the dreamer who has not yet woken

features.name: the light-pool
features.desc-on-touch: water that catches daylight and holds it without getting wet; inside it you see both the forest as it is and as it dreams itself; they are not different

features.name: the clearness-that-will-not-settle
features.desc-on-touch: this place has stopped allowing clarity and unclarity to be separate; you are as awake as you are asleep, the dream recognizes you are part of its own dreaming

inscription: the dream that continues without dreamers is the dream the forest has learned to be; it dreams itself awake each morning and does not sleep

file.name: Daylight_Dream_Journal_Never_Written.tmp
file.note: a record of dreams that persist into daytime; the archive cannot decide if these are dreams corrupting waking time or waking time learning to dream; the file expands during afternoon hours

exits.label: back deeper into the dream that does not end
toward waking—or deeper still into impossible clarity
along the animal-paths where creatures remember and forget together

reverie.title: REVERIE — clearing at noon, realization
narr: you're standing with her in a forest that is also sleeping.
she says: —do you think they know we're dreaming them?
you both realize at the same moment:
you've been inside this dream so long you forgot
whose eyes were doing the seeing. not yours. not hers.
